groups.summary: Confirmed on real headless Chromium 141. With config.autodiscover_targets=False, Chrome sends no TargetInfoChanged, TargetCreated or TargetDestroyed on the browser connection. So Browser.get and Tab.get(new_tab=True) always raise TimeoutError after the full timeout, although the navigation happened, and Tab.close always waits 10s and then raises TimeoutError although the tab closed. update_targets never prunes, so closed tabs stay in browser.tabs and main_tab, and browser.get then fails with 'No target with given id found'. Realism is low: autodiscover_targets is not a Config constructor parameter and is not documented. It is set to True in Config.__init__ and can only be overridden through **kwargs or attribute assignment, and its only user in the repo is a test that never calls get or close.

member_verdicts.note: browser.get(data url, timeout=3) raised TimeoutError after 3.01s, yet evaluate('document.title') returned 'hi'. browser.get(new_tab, timeout=3) raised TimeoutError after 3.02s, yet the tab exists at the new URL. tab.close() raised TimeoutError after 10.00s, and Target.getTargets no longer listed the closed tab.

Same run as B13.6. Both get paths raise TimeoutError after the timeout, and update_targets shows both tabs at their new URLs. Tab.get(new_tab=True) delegates to Browser.get, confirmed by reading Tab.get.
Same mechanism as B13.6 and A4.3. Severity is better described as wrong-result (TimeoutError raised although the operation succeeded) than crash.

With autodiscover off: closed the first tab with Target.closeTarget, then ran update_targets. Live pages were ['4F66DC'], but browser.tabs was ['6F2F21','C58E2B','4F66DC']. main_tab is the closed first tab, and browser.get raised ProtocolException 'No target with given id found' after 0.00s. With autodiscover on (the default), the TargetDestroyed handler prunes targets, so this needs autodiscover off (or otherwise missed events).

groups.refinements: This only matters to users who set the undocumented knob: cfg.autodiscover_targets=False, or zd.start(autodiscover_targets=False) through **kwargs. In the repo, only tests/core/test_browser.py::test_start_waits_for_initial_tab sets it, and that test only checks len(browser.tabs). With the knob set, get and close fail every time: the outcome is deterministic, not a race.

groups.summary: Confirmed on real headless Chromium 141. The headless UA override and the expert attachShadow patch are applied lazily, inside a Tab's first Connection.send. So the first document of a tab opened with Browser.get(new_tab=True), Browser.create_context(url), or window.open popups is requested with 'HeadlessChrome' in User-Agent, and page JS sees navigator.userAgent containing 'Headless'. The expert patch is also missing on that first document. The main tab is unaffected because Browser.get sends Page.navigate through the tab, which runs the preparation first. A reload of the new tab is clean.

member_verdicts.note: Server log (path, UA has HeadlessChrome, Sec-Fetch-Dest): /main-tab False; /new-tab True, and its JS beacon reported navigator.userAgent includes Headless = true; /ctx (create_context) True; /popup-open (window.open from the main tab) True; /new-tab after reload False. Expert mode: attachShadow({mode:'closed'}) yielded an open shadow root on /main-tab (open=true), not on the first /new-tab load (open=false), and did after reload (open=true). Sec-CH-UA had no 'Headless' in any case.

groups.evidence: r35_probe.py and r35_expert.py in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/BA-refute/. Code: Connection.send calls _prepare_expert/_prepare_headless only on the connection doing the send. Browser.get(new_tab) sends Target.createTarget(url) on the browser connection and then only waits for events, so the new Tab never sends before its first document loads. create_context does the same with createTarget(url, browser_context_id). The lazy design comes unchanged from upstream (5c1a005); 984bf02 only added client-hint metadata. test_headless_user_agent covers only browser.get on the main tab.
groups.refinements: Only affects headless=True (and expert=True for the shadow patch). It hits the first document, and its subresources and scripts, of tabs created with a URL by Chrome or zendriver without a prior send on the Tab: new_tab/new_window, create_context(url), and popups or target=_blank. Workaround: open the new tab at about:blank and then call tab.get(url). Passing Config(user_agent=...) sets --user-agent globally, which should also hide the token (assumed, not run). new_tab=True appears in docs/quickstart.md, so stealth users in headless mode can plausibly hit this.

groups.summary: All five members reproduce. The iteration protocol on Browser is broken in the edge cases: no page tabs gives AttributeError (also on real Chromium after closing every tab), only non-page targets gives ValueError, nested loops give AttributeError, zip(b, b) silently gives [(A, B)], next() after exhaustion gives AttributeError, and next(reversed(b)) gives TypeError. grant_all_permissions always fails on Chromium 141 with 'Unknown permission type: localNetwork', and four more types are rejected even when granted alone with an origin. tile_windows with the default max_columns uses about a third of the screen width in a single row, raises ZeroDivisionError with no windows, and never closes its mss instance. CookieJar.save and load regex-match str(cookie.__dict__), so common words select every cookie. Realism is low for most members. grant_all_permissions is the exception: it fails every time it is called.

member_verdicts.note: Offline Browser with hand-built targets: list(empty) and next(iter(empty), None) raise AttributeError '_i'. list(only service_worker) raises ValueError 'not in list'. Nested comprehension raises AttributeError. zip(b,b) gives [(A, B)]. next(it, 'sentinel') after list(it) raises AttributeError. next(reversed(b)) raises TypeError. Real Chromium: after closing all tabs, targets == [] and list(browser) raises AttributeError. The plain `for tab in browser:` loop used by examples/fetch_domain.py works, as does a re-loop after break. Realism is low: it needs zero page tabs, nested or parallel iteration, or iterator protocol misuse.

Real Chromium 141.0.7390.37: grant_all_permissions raised ProtocolException 'Unknown permission type: localNetwork'. Granting each type alone rejected handTracking, protectedMediaIdentifier, smartCard and webPrinting ("can't be granted in current context") plus localNetwork and loopbackNetwork (unknown). The same six fail with origin='https://example.com'. The single CAPTURED_SURFACE_CONTROL exclusion comes from upstream (5c1a005). Whether newer Chrome versions behave the same is not verified.

Fake mss with one 1920x1080 monitor and fake tabs: 1 window gives [[0,0,639,1080]], 2 give a total width of 638, 4 give 636 (159px each), 6 give 600 (100px each), always in one row. The default req_cols = int(n*19/6) comes from upstream. examples/demo.py mostly passes max_columns, which avoids it. Headful-only and rarely used, so realism is low.

tile_windows() with no tabs raises ZeroDivisionError at req_rows = int(num_windows / req_cols). 5 fake mss instances were created and 0 closed. Code reading of mss 10.0.0: linux.py calls XOpenDisplay in __init__ and XCloseDisplay only in close(); base.py has no __del__. Reaching the X client limit would take hundreds of calls, so realism is very low.

Offline CookieJar.save with cookies a=x, b=y and session_id=z: patterns 'session', 'secure', 'path', 'name', 'Medium', 'Secure', 'True', 'domain', 'x' and 'example' all saved all three cookies. '^a$' saved none, because anchors apply to the whole dict string. 'session_id' saved only the matching cookie. load() has the same loop. The existing test (pattern='nowsecure') passes only because that token does not appear in field names or enum reprs.
